about: The images and scans benchmark's corpus (scripts/parse-bench/images.mts). Other people's files: never committed. `npx tsx scripts/parse-bench/images.mts --fetch` downloads each into .bench/images/files/<id> and builds the references (images-ref.py). A pypi source is a member of that package's source archive; a raw source is a URL prefix; local is a file the PDF bench already keeps under .bench/real (its source is in corpus.json). A derived file is made by images-ref.py from fetched files, as `derived.how` says. Section a: PDFs, each labeled by looking at its pages (pdftoppm) and its text layer (pdftotext): article = the text layer holds the words (born-digital, slides, forms, a scan with a readable OCR layer); scan = printed or typed pages whose text layer is missing or does not hold the words; handwritten = notes, drawings, sketches. Section b: image files a reader might drop.
